newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO ENTER CLASH WITH PSG ON A ROLL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO ENTER CLASH WITH PSG ON A ROLL.

text.p: Monaco are on a roll that goes back to this time last year and, had they not made such a poor start to the 1995/6 campaign, their brilliant run-in to May would almost certainly have seen them crowned champions.
They are near unanimous favourites among the trainers of French first division clubs to win their sixth championship this season after entering the New Year four points clear.
They will consolidate that verdict if they beat their closest rivals Paris St Germain in their crunch match at Monaco's Louis II stadium on Sunday.
The statistics on previous clashes between the two sides at Louis II only make the Parisian club's task look all the more daunting.
PSG have not won a league match here since Monaco were promoted in 1977. Monaco's only home defeat by PSG in 20 years was 1-0 in the last 16 of the French Cup in 1993.
And the Parisians could not be coming to Monaco at a more troubled time in their short history.
They picked up only five points from their last six league games, allowing Monaco to overtake them at the top of the French first division in December.

A winter retreat to the tropics, where they were reported to have worked hard and improved squad solidarity, backfired badly with a 6-1 home defeat by Juventus in the first leg of the European Super Cup last week.
Concentration on Sunday's match in Monaco rather than the task in hand may have been partly to blame, but the shock has drained PSG's confidence.

"It's a defeat that will leave important traces," PSG's Brazilian coach Ricardo said. "One thing is sure, we're no longer the championship favourites. On January 26 at Monaco, we'll try to cause a surprise."
Monaco, their confidence sky high in contrast, will not contemplate anything other that winning the championship this season.
Club president Jean-Louis Campora said: "It's unthinkable that with the efforts that have been made, the quality of the players ... that we should fail."
"If the title escapes us it would be a huge disappointment," said Monaco's Brazilian striker Anderson, a player sought by Brazil-influenced PSG in the off-season.
Anderson lamented the lack of big football matches like Sunday's at Monaco and the lack of atmosphere at the Louis II stadium where average crowds last season were 6,000.
"They (PSG) are a team used to the big rendez-vous... Here it's different, we motivate each other. We can't count on our crowd. The stadium will no doubt be full, but what we need is to hear them."
Anderson scored when Monaco won their home league game against PSG 2-1 two years ago. He also scored the last time Monaco lost to PSG, a 2-1 defeat in Paris in September 1995.
The two sides drew 0-0 when they met in the capital in their first clash this season in September.
Tall libero Emmanuel Petit, back for Sunday's match after an injury layoff, scored the only goal when Monaco beat PSG at the Louis II stadium in February last year.
